cluster.headline: רגע אחד קפוא בזמן נשמר תקופה בלתי נתפסת של 99 מיליון שנה
cluster.body_note: Fetched via WebFetch (no JSON-LD articleBody; extracted via rendered text). Finding: an 8mm lizard tail preserved in amber, described as the earliest evidence for use of autotomy (voluntary tail drop to escape a predator). Amber excavated in northern Myanmar, geological layer dated to ~99 million years ago (mid-Cretaceous); no dating method named in the fetched excerpt. Researchers: Tel Aviv University, led by zoologist Dr. Leonidas-Romanos Davrazou and graduate student Dolev Pavrikant; micro-CT (X-ray) scan by Dr. Ahmed Nassar (Weizmann Institute) showing muscle arrangement consistent with a planned tail drop. Published in Palaeontologia Electronica, earlier this month (Oct 2026). Researchers believe the lizard was a distant relative of today's legless lizards (not snakes).
